notes.title: 23rd of September Update
notes.content:
Hello!



I've uploaded an update containing the following changes:

Item comparison is now implemented. Colored + and - icons will show next to attributes like range, damage or ship stats like armor and shield when viewing both weapons and modules. These icons show whether a stat is better or worse than the existing, already installed item. On weapons, hovering over an installed weapon will switch the comparison so it is always relative to the selected weapon. Note that not all attributes are compared: Set bonuses, perks, burst behaviour and ability values are still as-is. This change was one of the longest-requested from way back during private testing - I expect it will help ease some players into the loot game by taking a part of the cognitive load of item comparison off their shoulders.

Forge buffs have been updated to be exclusively bonus-based instead of the prior trade-off behaviour. While most forge buffs were already strict improvements, the upgrades to weapons contained trade-offs that made them much less desirable than almost all other upgrades. I have decided to remove the negative components from these upgrades entirely so that all forge buffs are now improvements with no drawbacks. This will make the choice of which buff to pick more engaging and raise player power by a small amount overall.

Material and scrap costs for upgrades have been slightly tweaked to make the health-related upgrades more affordable. Shield, armor and hull point upgrades have had their scalars reduced, meaning the increase in their scrap cost per upgrade purchased is reduced. The armor point upgrade has had its exotic matter cost converted to plasteel cost - this change is intended to address the pre-armor-regen early game situation, where flat armor is nearly useless compared to regen and no real choice is possible because both upgrades cost rare and valuable exotic matter. While armor regen will remain a crucial stepping stone in the transition from early to midgame, players can now invest into flat armor to make incremental survivability gains before the "big jump".

As always, please leave any feedback you have either in the discussion forums or on the discord, and I hope you have fun!

notes.title: 12th of September Update
notes.content:
Hello!



I just pushed an update with the following changes:

A weapon and module selection menu has been added after embarkation. This menu allows players to pick a weapon type for the first slot as well as spend credits (250 per) to start with a module in each slot. In addition, playing the tutorial now guarantees that the first weapon is a laser. This change was made to address the frustration of bad starting weapon RNG, particularly when spawning with all launchers. It should allow some mitigation of this issue as well as build planning when used in concert with some of the pre-embark temporary bonuses. While weapon selection is free, modules have a small credit cost to offset the power boost from weapon selection and provide a credit sink.

Resolution options have been tweaked to properly show the current running resolution as well as be visually coherent with the rest of the UI. The resolution dropdown now offers resolutions based on your display instead of the previous hand-written list.

Small UI tweaks have been made to improve tutorial flow and make the cruise button more "buttony".



There's also a secret change that allows the secret achievement to be earned, but obviously I can't say much more about that!



I hope you enjoy this update and feel that it makes your runs more consistent going forward.

notes.title: 7th of September Update: Photo Mode and New Achievements
notes.content:
Hello!

I've pushed a new build that includes the following new features and changes:

Photo Mode (returns): You can now enable a photo mode from the pause menu. In this mode you can move the camera freely using your controls for Pitch/Roll, Yaw, Throttle, View and Zoom. When activating photo mode, time stops and all UI elements are made invisible. Photo mode uses a traditional WASD+Mouselook setup for movement that may be awkward using custom keybinds, specific photo mode keybinds will come at a later date. Keep in mind that the modifier key used to rotate the camera in normal play is required to move the photo mode camera as well. The mode can be exited by using the respective pause menu option. Note that there is no built-in photo taking function, please use Steam's built-in screenshot option or other capture software. Be aware: Photo Mode has a technical limitation that I haven't yet been able to fix - when entering photo mode without having the sun in your field of view, its lens flare effect will be missing inside of photo mode. Conversely, when entering photo mode while having the sun in your field of view, its lens flare will be duplicated on the other side of the skybox. This is something I hope to be able to fix before release but remains an issue right now, so I decided to ship photo mode regardless.

New Achievements: I've added two new achievements: Navigator for those that defeat the demo's final boss, and Shipwright for those who unlock all ships in the demo. These will unlock retroactively, so if you've already done these things just start up the game and they should pop up. Regardless of how you unlock them, you may need to exit Catharage to get the Steam notification.

Dreadnought buffs: The Dreadnought has received a fifth weapon slot as well as slight buffs to its speed and maneuverability. This is intended to help it stand out as a more viable option next to the battleship and mothership, both of which have clearly identifiable strengths that the dreadnought has struggled to match. I'm collecting feedback on the ship-ship balancing and will tweak it further as release nears, so make sure to let me know what you think about your favourite (or least favourite) ships!

I hope you have fun with photo mode and can get some cool shots, and maybe chase one of the new achievements!

notes.title: End of August Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!



I just pushed an update containing a number of QOL and polish features:



Free floating scrap and credit chests now track to the player like materials do.

Scrapping loot now shows a preview of the potential scrap value gained. This value is now influenced by rarity, and most items are worth more. This should make it easier to gain scrap throughout normal play rather than just in large bursts when collecting Keystones.

Suspending now correctly stores and restores individual drone slots, meaning the Odachi hybrid battleship and runs with at least 2 Summoner set bonus points can be suspended without losing drone slots.

Targeting Overlay layering has been improved. Target Icons remain layered behind normal UI elements as they currently are but selecting them will move the expanded detail view in front of all other UI, making it no longer obstructed by things like weapon slots or the radial targeting menu.

Throttle and Agility UI has been altered to be bar-based instead of text-based. A two-bar display now sits where the Throttle Text used to be, reducing the reliance on numbers. Throttle and agility behaviour is unchanged.

Small UI tweaks include a unit display for weapons to show which unit fire delay is measured in (ticks for lasers, seconds for launchers/guns). In addition, the reset button has been moved from the pause menu to the main menu, distanced from other buttons and has had a confirmation window added to prevent accidental save game deletion. Module slots now show even if the module has no ability or set bonus.



I also want to touch one some changes that are currently work-in-progress but will arrive before launch (and ideally quite soon):

-comparison mode between new and old items is proving more complicated than anticipated and will be coming in a future update

-individual axis steering adjustments for outlier ships like the Destroyer is incoming, but not finalized as this is a very "deep" change that touches many systems

-a "reverse" throttle mode is potentially coming, depending on whether I can figure out how to make it work with trails properly - there's some work that needs to be done with trails as is

-cruise particle issues persist with certain ships, and this is an issue that I currently cannot reproduce so it remains difficult to solve



That's all for today, I hope you enjoy the new update!

notes.title: Demo Update: New Suspend Feature, Camera Controls & More
notes.content:
Hey everyone,



I just pushed a major update to the demo, based on player feedback and outstanding fixes and goals:



Suspend Feature: I've added a new option to the pause menu called "suspend & quit" that allows you to save elements of your current run to resume later. This button will save your current ship, all equipment (weapons & modules) and its stats including set bonuses. Your collected currency is also saved and restored. Fleet members you have recruited will not rejoin you. The suspend option is available from your first warp onward. If a suspended state is available, the "embark" option in the main menu will be replaced with a "suspend" option that will spawn you in the training area with your recovered ship, currency and items. While I've tested this system and already fixed a whole heap of new and exotic errors that came with it, some edge cases may still exist where stats or items are not saved and restored correctly. If you come across these, please report to me (with details) so I can investigate.



Fighter Cam Orbit Rotation: The "Fighter Cam" now allows for camera orbit rotation just like the main game cam. Press your camera orbit key (default Right Mouse Button) and move the mouse to rotate this view. These new controls respect the inversion and sensitivity settings in the options menu just like the main camera rotation does.



Persistence for Button Guide toggle: The game now saves the state of the Button Guide menu, meaning you don't have to toggle it every time you start.



I hope you enjoy these new features and get some long runs going, and if you've struggled with the movement and camera before, maybe the new controls can help you!

notes.title: Demo Bugfixes and QOL Update
notes.content:
I've just uploaded a small demo update addressing some outstanding bugs and implementing feedback.



Changelog

fixed a bug where fleet members would show up on the targeting display despite being dead

camera switching is now possible from all states to all other states

sensor contact health display has been made independent from cursor hover state and can be viewed without hovering, as long as sensor solution is strong enough. This display is scaled by distance but will become full-size when hovered

added an "all weapons" button that assigns all weapons to the target

added text status displays under weapons that show the current state, such as tracking, firing, reloading and more



I'm continuously collecting feedback and will continue to update the demo with changes and bugfixes. If you have feedback or suggestions, please post them either on the Steam discussion board or the game's Discord.
